decisions.executionNote: Coin is in left workspace, bank on right. Begin elbow-up left approach with open gripper; refine position from wrist view.
Continue smooth left elbow-up rotation toward downward coin grasp, advancing toward the visually farther holder.
Continuity guard stopped after one step; reduce rotation and advancement and replan from measured pose.
Continue approach toward holder with downward-facing fingers; gradual rotation maintains elbow-up branch.
Finish most of the downward alignment while advancing over the left holder; final grasp alignment remains visual.
Use wrist view to center the coin, correcting lateral offset and final downward orientation before closing.
Coin remains left of the wrist grasp center. Shift forward with a small tilt correction, keeping jaws open for visual alignment.
Coin is nearly centered between the open jaws. Make a small lateral/depth correction and begin a controlled pinch.
Pause closure and correct the remaining wrist-image offset with a small pure translation; verify alignment before grasping.
Observed translation moved the coin farther off center. Reopen slightly and reverse that correction, also centering grasp depth without lowering.
Coin appears tilted after contact but remains within the jaw opening. Center slightly and close carefully; retention will be checked on lift.
Coin slipped out to the right of the holder during closure. Reopen and lift clear to observe its resting position for recovery.
Recover the dropped coin from the table in the left workspace. Move above its RGB location and orient the open jaws vertically for a rim grasp.
Servo over the flat coin using the downward wrist image, translating toward its center while staying above the table.
Coin is centered in wrist view. Descend vertically with open jaws, preserving orientation, to approach its rim.
Correct the depth-dependent wrist offset toward the flat coin, reducing the jaw opening while still above contact.
Approach the flat coin rim with small downward steps and correct remaining wrist-image depth offset, keeping fingers separated.
Flat coin is now centered at the fingertips. Lower only a few millimeters and close around its rim to attempt recovery.
Close fully and make a short vertical lift to test whether the coin is retained by the rim.
The coin was not retained and moved away from the jaw tips. Reopen and recenter over its resting position before another rim grasp.
The coin is horizontally centered. Descend with fixed orientation and open jaws to put the rim at the finger contact height.
Lower to the flat rim with a compensating small depth translation; keep jaws separated until both tips are at the coin height.
Tracking indicates table contact, so stop descending. Make a tiny centering correction and close around the coin rim at the current height.
Complete closure and lift slowly to test the rim grasp, checking coin retention in the wrist image.
Raise further with the gripper closed and inspect whether the coin moves rigidly with the hand or remains on the table.
Coin stayed on the table. Reopen and approach with its center deeper between the finger pads rather than beyond the tips.
Descend near the table while keeping the coin deeper between both pads; make only millimeter lateral corrections.
Coin is centered behind the finger tips at table height. Hold pose and close symmetrically around the rim.
The rim now overlaps both pads. Keep the grip fully closed and test retention with a slow short lift.
Maintain closure and raise clear of the table to verify a stable lift before attempting transfer.
Top-down rim attempts have not retained the coin. Change to a shallow side approach so the jaws can pinch its upper and lower faces.
The continuity guard rejected the approach without movement. Halve the rotation and translation increments while maintaining the elbow-up branch.
Continue the side-grasp reorientation in small continuous increments, keeping the jaws clear of the flat coin.
Continue toward the coin edge, correcting world lateral alignment while rotating toward a nearly horizontal face pinch.
Lower the side-oriented gripper while retaining configuration continuity; the coin remains on the table and offset below the current grasp axis.
Replan from the guarded pose with smaller steps. Bring the lower jaw toward table level for a shallow face pinch.
Contact prevented further lowering. Back away slightly, narrow the vertical jaw gap, and flatten the side approach before trying to slide onto the rim.
Lower the narrowed side-grasp carefully toward the table, monitoring tracking and keeping configuration continuity.
Side approach is constrained by table contact. Raise and steepen the fingers to a diagonal rim pinch while advancing closer to the coin.
Continue the diagonal approach, moving the fingertips toward the coin while lifting the wrist clear of the table.
Lower the diagonal jaw opening toward the coin edge, with a small retreat to keep the lower finger clear.
The coin has tilted against the lower finger. Shift the opening onto the tilted rim and start a controlled face pinch without further downward loading.
Close on the tilted coin at the lower jaw and make a very short retention-test lift.
Raise the closed diagonal grasp and inspect whether the coin stays fixed relative to the fingertips.
The coin did not stay with the fingers. Reposition the diagonal jaw opening farther onto its near rim, correcting the visible lateral miss.
Move the opening onto the visible near rim with millimeter corrections; keep it open until the coin overlaps both contact faces.
The tilted rim now lies between both tips. Close without lateral movement, then lift slightly to test the pinch.
A coin edge is visible between the closed pads. Lift vertically without changing orientation to verify retention.
The coin stayed on the table. Reopen and lower the diagonal grasp closer to the actual rim height, using the head view to correct the approach position.
Lower the diagonal opening toward the coin's true table height, without closing prematurely; monitor for contact.
Table contact limits descent. Shift onto the near edge while closing and slightly lowering the center as the lower jaw retracts.
Coin remains outside the closed tips. Reopen and move the opening across its near rim while lifting enough to avoid table loading.
Shift the still-open jaws farther around the visible coin edge, aiming for overlap behind both finger tips before closure.
Coin is centered with its rim overlapping the finger region. Close at a fixed pose before a separate lift test.
Keep the pinch closed and lift two centimeters to check whether the coin remains fixed between the pads.
The coin again remained on the table. Clear the surface and realign above its head-camera location for a more accurate downward rim grasp.
Continue rotating downward above the coin with an open gripper and smooth elbow-up motion.
Bring the open fingers nearly vertical over the coin, compensating the fingertip offset as the wrist rotates.
Align the vertical fingertips with the coin's calibrated table position and descend near rim height with the jaws open.
Correct the last few millimeters while lowering to rim height and gradually close, avoiding a large table-loading motion.
Hold full closure on the visibly overlapped rim, then perform a slow one-centimeter lift to assess retention.
Coin appears stable between both pads after the short lift. Raise it well clear of the holder/table while maintaining full closure.
Coin is visibly retained. Raise and rotate it toward a vertical center handover, keeping the left arm in its workspace and the grip closed.
